_comment: Canonical source for the OpenAI Plugins Directory listing. Consumed by build/assemble.py when generating .codex-plugin/plugin.json; nothing here is hand-copied into that manifest. Identity fields (name, version, description, license, keywords, skills) still come from core/skill-meta.json -- this file carries ONLY the publisher identity and the consumer-facing listing copy.

_note.candidate_count_omitted: The README says how many candidates the protocol generates and how many a critic typically kills. Those numbers are deliberately absent from every field here. In README context they read as a description of the method; in store copy a number reads as a result -- a claim about what the user will get -- and we have no measurement that supports reading it that way. Architecture words are out for the same reason: a listing describes what the thing does for the reader, not how it is built.

interface.longDescription:
Innovate or Die is a staged workflow for problems where the conventional answer is already known and the value lies in what everyone has overlooked.

Instead of answering in one pass, it works the problem in stages. It restates what is actually being asked and names the obvious answer up front, so that answer cannot be handed back as though it were a discovery. It opens a wide field of candidate approaches, each carrying the mechanism that would make it work. It then attacks that field: sorting ideas that are genuinely new from familiar advice in unfamiliar words, and separating the constraints that are real from the ones that were inherited and never checked. What survives is reopened and pushed to its more radical version, then scored against a quality gate before any of it reaches you.

What comes back is the strongest thesis first, a reframing of the problem, the opportunities worth pursuing with the mechanism behind each, the most contrarian hypothesis on the table, the cheapest test that would prove that hypothesis wrong, a short list of what was rejected and why, and an honest statement of what may still be missing.

It is built to hold its ground on two things. When the conventional answer really is the best one available, it is instructed to say so rather than manufacture novelty. And when an idea depends on a price, a figure, or a regulation it was never given, it names what you need to look up instead of inventing something plausible.

Ask it something hard -- a strategy, pricing, product, growth, or architecture question you have already thought about and got nowhere with -- or just say "innovate or die". It is deliberately the wrong tool for two jobs: choosing between options you have already defined, and carrying out a plan you have already made.

Created by Ken Pendergast. Published on OpenAI by PESTalytix LLC.
capabilities: Generate non-obvious opportunities, each with the mechanism that would make it work
Challenge the assumptions a problem statement takes for granted
Stress-test a proposed idea for real novelty and for what would falsify it
Design cheap experiments with a pass/fail number set before the test runs
defaultPrompt: Find a non-obvious solution to this problem.
Challenge the assumptions behind this strategy.
Turn this idea into falsifiable experiments.
